subject: Compact evaluation corridor & fallback proposal
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@medicron.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Compact evaluation corridor & fallback proposal

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. I promised to capture a short, operational proposal so your procurement and engineering teams have a clear path if the initial acceptance window tightens.

Key ask: can your team confirm whether the evaluation gate needs the full 4-week window (as in the SOW) or whether we have flexibility to compress to a 10-business-day corridor with parallel validation? If procurement insists on the full window, we’ll need to trigger the fallback (credit + extended support) outlined below to preserve the target close date.

At a glance:
- Compact corridor (preferred): 10 business days of focused validation, with our onboarding engineers on-call and a dedicated verification checklist.
- Fallback lane (if procurement requires extra vendor approval): automatic 14-day extension + $XK service credit + two-hour executive review cadence.
- Trigger: procurement or security questionnaire outstanding beyond 3 business days after delivery of evidence package.

Attached: MAP_Draft_Medicron_v1.pdf (draft MAP with milestones, owners, and triggers).

Next steps:
1) Alice — confirm whether the 10-day corridor is feasible with your stakeholders by EOD Friday.
2) If not, we’ll mark the fallback lane and prepare the credit paperwork.

Appreciate your partnership — I’m cc’ing Camila and Marissa to stay aligned on sequencing and credits.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
M: (415) 555-0123
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Cc: Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@medicron.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-30T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact evaluation corridor & fallback proposal

Mina — thanks for the clear write-up and the MAP. High level: procurement just flagged two points that will likely push the window out if not resolved quickly: SOC 2 evidence review and legal's data retention clause. Ben (copied) is leading procurement and wants to see the exact evidence package.

We can try the 10-business-day corridor but I need to confirm with security whether they can run parallel review on day 1–5 while the integration team does functional tests. If security agrees to parallelize, we can keep the close date. If not, procurement will request the longer timeline.

I've attached our proposed procurement timeline (Procurement_Timeline.xlsx) — it shows a conservative path and an accelerated path. I’ll push for the accelerated path but can’t promise it yet.

I’ll get back with a firm answer by Thursday EOD. If we need the fallback lane, we’ll request the credit details in writing.

Best,
Alice Park
VP of Partnerships | Medicron Health
alice@medicron.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact evaluation corridor & fallback proposal

Looping back with a quick internal remediation plan in case Medicron cannot compress:

Option A (compact corridor — best economic outcome):
- We pre-stage evidence bundle today (SOC 2 attestation excerpts, ingestion-minimal retention plan, audit log sample).
- On-call engineering for 10-business-day corridor; daily standups with Medicron eng lead.
- No credit required if parallel review accepted.

Option B (fallback lane — preserves momentum but costs slightly):
- Trigger automatic 14-day extension from the originally scheduled acceptance start.
- Apply a $12,000 account credit (one-time) tied to delay; Redwood will also provide two weeks of prioritized onboarding time.
- Execute a short addendum (one page) to the MAP to document the trigger and the credit.

Action items for us:
- Mina: prep a bundled evidence packet and send by EOD.
- Marissa: draft the one-page addendum and credit memo so it’s ready if Ben requests it.
- Jonas: stand by for executive review if Medicron asks for a senior-level signoff.

I’ll draft both the pre-staged evidence checklist and the addendum template and circulate by lunchtime.

-Camila
Camila Reyes
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@medicron.com>, Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@medicron.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact evaluation corridor & fallback proposal

Alice / Ben — following up with the updated MAP and a clear trigger table so your procurement and security teams can make a single, binary decision: accelerate (10-day corridor) or accept fallback (14-day extension + credit).

What I attached: Updated_MAP_Medicron_v2.pdf — includes:
- A concise evidence index (SOC 2 excerpts, retention policy summary, sample audit log export).
- Trigger table: specific thresholds (e.g., outstanding questionnaire >72 hours) that auto-select the fallback lane.
- One-page addendum template for the credit (ready to sign).

Request: Please confirm which path you prefer by Thursday, 2028-07-05 COB so we can lock resources and finalize the MPA. If you confirm the compact corridor, we’ll begin the pre-staged evidence handoff on Monday and schedule daily 30-minute verification calls. If fallback is chosen, we’ll circulate the addendum and process the credit authorization.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456 (addendum/credit).

Small ask to Ben: if procurement can provision a point person to clear evidence items within 48 hours of receipt, we will be able to avoid the fallback in most cases.

Thanks all — open to a quick sync if you want to run through the trigger table.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
